_comment: Every entity key retired by the gpt 5.6 tier re-key and by the redundant leading-token strip that follows it, pinned against the MEASURED outcome rather than a uniform expectation. Two levers, one retired set: the tier re-key moves luna/sol/terra from being families of their own to being variants of family `gpt`, and the leading-token strip drops an id's first token when — and only when — another axis already carries the fact it names, which lets the version scan reach versions it had been starting one token late for. Each case carries the MEASURED migration record: `retired_instances` is the exact set of provider instances the key held immediately before the levers (spelled `<provider>|<model id>`, read off the pre-lever generated catalog), and `successors` is the set of entity keys those instances now belong to, RE-DERIVED from the instances on every run rather than claimed in prose. The CHANGELOG migration table is compared against this record too, so the three copies cannot drift apart silently. THREE rows record a MEASURED DEVIATION from the epoch-wide `show`-seam expectation: `ministral#3b{instruct}`, `mistral/large#675b{instruct}` and `nemotron#120b` still RESOLVE there, because each remains a valid under-specified reference to exactly one live entity. Nothing was added to make a retired key resolve — the exact-key seam (`--by-entity`) is a hard 404 for all 26 — and 'fixing' these into 404s would break ordinary under-specified lookups, which is the same hazard the bare-family ambiguity carve-out exists to protect. See TESTING.md.

provenance.ref: the epoch-wide retired-key policy: a retired entity key is a uniform hard 404 on the exact-key seam — no alias, no redirect, no successor listing. The CHANGELOG old->new table is the only pointer a user gets.

mutation.description: LucidQuery serves both of its AGI rows as `lucidquery-agi-01-…`, repeating its own provider slug in front of the model name. With the redundant leading token gone the remainder names the release the vendor published — AGI-01 — so the bare `agi` key was never the artifact's identity, only the residue of a version the scan could not reach. A pure rename: both instances move together and the bare `agi` FAMILY stays live, which is why the `show` seam reports an ambiguity rather than a 404.

mutation.description: amazon-bedrock's `mistral.ministral-3-3b-instruct`. The `mistral.` segment names the creating lab; behind it sits the generation `3`. MEASURED DEVIATION from the epoch policy's `show` arm: this string still RESOLVES on the looser `show` seam, because it remains a valid UNDER-SPECIFIED reference to the single live `ministral@3#3b{instruct}` entity. It is not an alias and not a redirect — no instrument was added to make a retired key resolve; the ordinary resolver simply finds one match for a ref that names fewer fields than the key does. The exact-key seam (`--by-entity`) is a hard 404, which is the arm the policy is about.

mutation.description: amazon-bedrock's `mistral.mistral-large-3-675b-instruct` — here the creator token and the family token are the same word, and the carrier check licenses the strip because family `mistral` genuinely declares creator `mistral`. The generation `3` behind it becomes reachable. The harvested HuggingFace repo `mistralai/Mistral-Large-3-675B-Instruct-2512` pointed at this key and is re-pointed at the successor in the same change. MEASURED DEVIATION on the `show` seam, same shape as the ministral 3b row: the string stays a valid under-specified reference to one live entity. RE-MEASURED at the 2026-08-28 models.dev catalog refresh (providers 170 -> 204, provider model rows 5,765 -> 7,430): the `show` seam moved from RESOLVED to the under-specified reading. Nothing about the lever changed and the successor is still `mistral/large@3#675b{instruct}` — that ONE entity simply gained two more provider rows (nano-gpt and nvidia joined amazon-bedrock), and they group into two distinct date-differentiated candidates. So this key leaves the "resolves to one live entity" class and joins the ordinary single-entity date-fragmentation class that `kimi{instruct}` is already filed under. The exact-key seam is still a hard 404
